common_name: Wildfire Camellia (Vivid Orange-Red Semi-Double Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; Wildfire's large semi-double flowers open earlier in the season than many red japonica cultivars, so siting under high tree canopy helps protect buds from late cold snaps.

directions: Originating from a Nuccio's Nurseries seedling in California, Wildfire produces vivid orange-red semi-double flowers roughly four inches across with a prominent center of golden stamens, blooming in early to mid season on a vigorous, upright evergreen shrub. The intensity of the flower color reads especially well against the plant's own glossy dark-green foliage or sited in front of a lighter background wall or hedge. Grow in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil with reliable drainage, and protect from harsh afternoon sun, which can bleach the saturated flower color and scorch the leaves. Prune only right after bloom to shape, since next season's flower buds form on the current year's growth.

common_name: Mrs. Bertha A. Harms Camellia (Large White Semi-Double Camellia japonica with Pink Blush)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; this older Pacific Northwest selection, also sold as 'Auburn White,' needs room to develop its naturally open, upright framework.

directions: A long-cultivated heirloom camellia traced to around 1900, Mrs. Bertha A. Harms bears large, semi-double white flowers with a faint pink cast and a showy cluster of long golden stamens, opening from midseason into late season. The open, upright growth habit is looser than many compact modern japonica cultivars, giving it a more naturalistic, large-shrub presence in a woodland border. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, and mulch heavily to protect the shallow root system through summer heat. This cultivar has also been used as a breeding parent for later fragrant camellia hybrids, reflecting its continued value in camellia collections.

common_name: Benten Camellia (Variegated Yellow-Margined Rose-Red Camellia japonica)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, strongly acidic soil in partial shade; grown chiefly as a foliage specimen, Benten is best sited where its unusual variegated, crinkle-edged leaves can be viewed up close.

directions: A historic Japanese heirloom exported to the West in the 1930s, Benten is grown mainly for its distinctive variegated foliage — leaves with irregular yellow margins and a puckered, deformed edge quite unlike the smooth, solid-green leaves of typical japonica cultivars. It produces comparatively modest small, single, rose-red flowers in midseason, a secondary feature next to the year-round foliage interest. Grow in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, protected from harsh afternoon sun that can scorch the variegated leaf margins, and remove any shoots that revert to solid green to preserve the pattern.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Interstella flowers earlier than many older Pieris cultivars, so a sheltered site helps protect the first flush of buds from hard late frosts.

directions: Bred by Maryland breeder Mike Farrow and introduced through the Proven Winners ColorChoice line, Interstella opens very early in spring with large, drooping clusters of ruby-pink, bell-shaped flowers, paired with new growth that emerges in bright red and orange tones. Its upright, mounding habit stays compact at roughly three to four feet, making it a manageable choice for a foundation planting or shaded border without the eventual bulk of older seedling-grown Pieris. Grow in moist, humus-rich, strongly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, and shelter from harsh winter wind, which can brown both the evergreen foliage and the overwintering flower buds. Deer tend to leave the foliage alone, making it a practical choice where browse pressure limits other shade shrubs.

common_name: Pink Frost Pieris (Passion Party Series Variegated Pink-Flowered Andromeda)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade, siting it where the creamy-edged foliage and pink spring flowers are both visible at close range.

directions: Part of the Dutch Passion Party series, Pink Frost pairs deep green leaves edged in creamy yellow with profuse clusters of light pinkish-red, bell-shaped flowers that fade to a frosty pink-blushed white as they age, giving the plant a two-tone bloom display over several weeks. Its strong branching and compact, well-filled habit set it apart from older, more open-growing variegated Pieris selections, and breeders selected it in part for improved resistance to common Pieris diseases. Grow in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter wind and afternoon sun that can scorch the pale leaf margins, and remove any reverted all-green shoots to keep the variegation crisp.
